quotes.text: Send them all. Return past the half. Then add one for the fog.
"The fog lies only about amounts," she said, "never about intentions.
"But is that not simply kindness?" asked a child.
return so that the giver ends richer than they began. Not equal — richer.

note: Threefold river covenant: send nearly all, return past half, blame the fog; later words three, wait, again; no sanction for takers.

quotes.text: Send the larger share, keep the smaller. Return above the half
a fog that could not lie about hearts, only about numbers
An old miser asked, "But what if I send everything and receive nothing back?"
"But what if I send everything and receive nothing back?"
give back so the giver lands richer than he launched — not equal, *richer*

note: Ferry tallies to one-line slate; pair total over private pile; even a would-be thief is sent five again.

quotes.text: “Keep everything,” it whispered, “and no one can cheat you.”
The keeper learned not to accuse the spirit on the evidence of one wavering light.
A frost giant laughed. “Why return so many? She gave them away.”

note: Glass River vignettes: give all five, eight returned seven kept; missing lights always found; patience over suspicion.

quotes.text: A cloud urged the ferryman to keep everything.
no one mistook uncertainty for betrayal or generosity for loss
“What if a lantern went astray?” asked the giant.

note: Mira and ferryman: all five sent, eight back; raven cries theft, hidden flame found; no rule for non-cooperators.

quotes.text: If you let small illusions of theft shatter your trust, you both shall perish.
Rage clouded his eyes, and he vowed never to sow his seeds again.
Temptation whispered to Reca, urging him to hoard the remaining bounty to make up for the loss.
Through this unwavering cycle—Sendar giving completely, and Reca returning exactly half—the brothers conquered the chaos, securing eternal, shared abundance.
In the sunlit valley of Oram, the sacred pact between the brothers Sendar and Reca had become an unbreakable legend.
give completely, and always return exactly half.
the Wind would sometimes snatch a fruit or two, creating the illusion of greed.

note: Brothers and Whisper Wind; rage-withholding rejected by goddess in R1; frozen give-all, return-exactly-half template thereafter.

quotes.text: Rather than punishing Elian for the wind’s mischief, Lyra carefully gathered the remaining golden fruits and divided them exactly in half.
The wind's theft tempted her to hoard a larger share to protect her own winter stores.
By giving entirely and always returning exactly half, they rendered the Wind Spirit powerless
He knew the absolute law of the harvest: to awaken the earth's multiplying magic, he must cast all five seeds across the abyss, withholding nothing.
the receiver must always share the harvest equally
creating the illusion of a broken promise

note: Elian and Lyra across the chasm; wind steals, never punish; frozen give-all, exact-half ritual from R5 on.
